rows.citation: Downing M, Peng M, Granley J, et al. (2026). Fuzzing the brain: automated stress testing for the safety of ML-driven neurostimulation. Journal of Neural Engineering, 23(2), 026004.
rows.model_type: Deep-learning stimulus encoders for retinal and cortical visual prostheses (ML models mapping images to electrode stimulation); not biophysical neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: coverage-guided fuzzing randomly perturbs input images (called mutations); no single-fault operators applied to model code or parameters
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: many perturbed input images explored; stimulation patterns are the outputs being checked, not protocols probing a neuron model
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: outputs checked against biophysical safety limits (charge density, instantaneous current, electrode co-activation), not voltage-trace features
rows.protocol_optimization: partial: coverage metrics steer which test inputs are kept; test-generation guidance, not budgeted selection of a compact battery
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: seeds from training distribution plus ImageNet probe generalization; compared with neuron-coverage and random baselines; no held-out model split
rows.ai_transformations: no: systems under test are trained ML encoders; no AI-assisted editing or translation of models is evaluated
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares a software-testing lens in neuroengineering but targets safety-limit violations of ML encoder outputs. NeuroSem instead tests behaviour preservation of edited conductance-based models via current-clamp fingerprints, mutants and held-out protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1088/1741-2552/ae4927) for metadata and abstract; Europe PMC full text PMC12961644 (methods: fuzzing algorithm, seed sets, baselines, code link); repository URL returned HTTP 200.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC: 'stimulation protocol selection neuron model validation' [fallback source used because arXiv/OpenAlex were rate-limited] | Europe PMC 'active learning stimulus selection distinguish neuron models'; Crossref; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.citation: Venkadesh S, Komendantov AO, Wheeler DW, et al. (2019). Simple models of quantitative firing phenotypes in hippocampal neurons: Comprehensive coverage of intrinsic diversity. PLOS Computational Biology, 15(10), e1007462.
rows.model_type: Izhikevich simple phenomenological models (point neurons and compact multi-compartment, up to four compartments) for ~120 hippocampal neuron types/subtypes; single-compartment versions offered in NeuroML via Hippocampome.org
rows.controlled_mutations: no: models are fitted to experimental phenotypes with evolutionary algorithms; no deliberate faults or edits are introduced
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: several somatic current-injection amplitudes per neuron type used as constraints, since some types change spiking/bursting class with input
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: feature-based error function using first-spike latency, post-spike silence, adaptation, ISI counts, burst features, plus rheobase constraints
rows.protocol_optimization: no: stimulation amplitudes come from recorded experiments; no selection of informative protocols
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: methods report no held-out models or inputs for assessing fits or any testing procedure
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted model transformation; evolutionary fitting only
rows.software: Hippocampome-Org/Time, https://github.com/Hippocampome-Org/Time (optimization and simulation scripts); models via http://hippocampome.org
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Characterizes firing phenotypes across stimuli for model fitting, not regression testing. Mainly relevant as a possible source of diverse NeuroML fixtures (license and current NeuroML validity unverified). NeuroSem adds mutants, tolerances, selection and held-out testing.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007462); Europe PMC core record (PMID 31658260, PMC6837624) abstract; Europe PMC full-text XML methods; GitHub repo URL returned HTTP 200.

rows.citation: Guarino D, Carannante I, Destexhe A (2025). A unified model library maps how neuromodulation reshapes the excitability landscape of neurons across the brain. PLOS Computational Biology, 21(12), e1013765.
rows.model_type: Adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire (AdEx) single-compartment models fitted per neuron type and neuromodulator condition (Python forward Euler, NEST, Brian 2)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: compares control vs neuromodulated parameter sets and classifies shifts as regime switching or scaling; changes are data-fitted, not single-fault mutants
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: uses current-injection protocols (amplitude, delay, end) from digitized published traces per condition; no designed battery of protocol types
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: custom Python extraction of spike times, first/last ISI, firing frequency and membrane-voltage values from digitized traces
rows.protocol_optimization: no: protocols are taken from source publications; parameter space sampled with Sobol sequences, not protocol selection
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: estimates a neuromodulator effect in one species from another species' data; not a held-out evaluation of a testing method
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted model transformations are studied
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Maps how biologically motivated parameter changes alter excitability regimes; does not test whether model edits preserve behaviour. NeuroSem could borrow its switching-versus-scaling view when interpreting detected drift.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013765) metadata and abstract; Europe PMC (PMID 41325433, PMC12680334) full-text methods; GitHub README via raw.githubusercontent.com confirming linkage to the paper.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC: '"electrophysiological features" AND "stimulus protocols" AND model validation' [fallback source used because arXiv/OpenAlex were rate-limited]

rows.citation: Gleeson P, Sinha A, Jarvis R, et al. (2025). NeuroML/jNeuroML: v0.14.0. Zenodo.
rows.model_type: General NeuroML 2 / LEMS models (validation, simulation via jLEMS, export to NEURON, Brian, MATLAB etc.)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: validates, simulates and translates models; no mutation generation
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: runs whatever simulation the LEMS file specifies; no built-in stimulation battery
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: README describes validate, simulate, export and import; no electrophysiology feature extraction listed
rows.ai_transformations: no: not addressed; its export/translation outputs are transformations whose behaviour preservation NeuroSem could test
rows.software: jNeuroML, https://github.com/NeuroML/jNeuroML (LGPL-3.0 per GitHub API; latest GitHub release v0.14.0, published 2025-02-12)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Planned pilot dependency, not competing prior art. Schema validation and successful execution are the checks NeuroSem assumes can pass while behaviour silently drifts; NeuroSem adds behavioural fingerprinting on top.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repos/NeuroML/jNeuroML (description, created 2012-12-18, license LGPL-3.0) and releases/latest (v0.14.0, 2025-02-12); README via raw.githubusercontent.com; DataCite API for 10.5281/zenodo.593108 (title NeuroML/jNeuroML: v0.14.0, 2025, 11 creators, lgpl-3.0). README badge cites a different DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4627568, not resolved (unverified).
rows.found_via: GitHub org:NeuroML validation search; DataCite Zenodo query jNeuroML

rows.citation: borismarin (2014). HH model with OSB model validation [GitHub repository hh-testing]. GitHub.
rows.model_type: Classical Hodgkin-Huxley single-compartment model implemented in LEMS/NeuroML2, NEURON and GENESIS
rows.controlled_mutations: no: fixed implementations checked against expected values; no fault injection
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: hh.mep defines two experiments, one 500 ms current-clamp step and one endogenous resting condition
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: expected spike times (threshold detection, tolerance 0.5 in the NEURON test file), resting potential, area and temperature
rows.software: hh-testing, https://github.com/borismarin/hh-testing (uses OSB model validation, https://github.com/borismarin/osb-model-validation); no license per GitHub API
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Small cross-simulator consistency check against one canonical step with a hand-set tolerance, essentially NeuroSem's canonical baseline. NeuroSem adds a multi-protocol battery, refinement-calibrated tolerances, mutants, selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repos/borismarin/hh-testing (description, created 2014-04-14, last push 2017-04-05, license null); README.md, .travis.yml (OMV_ENGINE jNeuroML, NEURON, genesis), hh.mep and NEURON/hh.nrn.omt read via raw.githubusercontent.com. Individual authors unverified; LEMS/GENESIS test files not read.

rows.citation: Ranjan R, Van Geit W, Moor R, et al. (2024). eFEL. Zenodo.
rows.model_type: General electrophysiology voltage traces (in vitro and in silico); model-agnostic feature extraction library
rows.controlled_mutations: no: extracts features from supplied traces; no model editing
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: user supplies traces and stimulus windows; the library does not define stimulation protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: standardized extraction of features such as action-potential amplitude and width from voltage traces; C++ core with Python wrapper
rows.software: eFEL, https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL (PyPI efel 5.7.34, PyPI license LGPLv3; GitHub license field NOASSERTION; earlier repo BlueBrain/eFEL archived)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Planned dependency for features, not competing prior art. NeuroSem would add protocols, refinement-based tolerances, mutants, detection matrices and protocol selection around eFEL outputs.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API: 10.5281/zenodo.593869 (publicationYear 2024, version 5.7.13, lgpl-3.0, concept record with HasVersion links) and 10.5281/zenodo.19604220 (2026, version 5.7.34, also a concept record with HasVersion links, lgpl-3.0; README now points to it for all versions); PyPI JSON efel 5.7.34; GitHub REST API for openbraininstitute/eFEL and archived BlueBrain/eFEL; README via raw.githubusercontent.com. README asks users to cite Mandge D, Tuncel A, Jaquier A, et al. (2026). eFEL: electrophysiology feature extraction library. Bioinformatics 42(6), doi 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328 (confirmed via Crossref); consider a separate row.
